subtype: Approach: rehearses a speech in the mind and in front of a mirror [Action]
passage: After school, Jahnavi stood in front of the tall mirror in the dance room, with her talk about honeybees due on Monday. First she closed her eyes and pictured the classroom: the teacher by the window, everyone sitting on the floor mats, herself beside the board. Then she opened her eyes and said her first line to the mirror. "Good morning, today I will tell you how bees talk without a single word." It came out smooth. The second point, how bees dance to show where the flowers are, vanished. She stopped, frowned and tried again. The same gap. So she stuck a note reading DANCE on the corner of the mirror. Varun, waiting his turn to use the room, peeked in. "Again?" "Again," said Jahnavi.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi feeling when the second point vanished?
qa.a: Jahnavi felt frustrated and a little worried, shown by her frown and by trying again.

qa.q: What else could Jahnavi try to remember the second point?
qa.a: Jahnavi could practise with a friend listening, or draw a small dancing bee as a cue card, since a picture can help her remember.

qa.q: How might Varun see Jahnavi's rehearsal?
qa.a: Varun might find it funny that Jahnavi is practising again, but could also see that practising is how the gap was found.

grounding: Shows a girl imagining the room, rehearsing her opening line in a mirror and spotting where the second point slips away.

subtype: Approach: rehearses a speech in the mind and in front of a mirror [Action]
passage:
I'm Jeevan, and my sister Deepika had to give a two-minute talk on turtles in class on Monday.
On Saturday she sat on the bed with her eyes shut, whispering. "I'm pretending I'm in class," she said. "Everyone looking at me."
Then she stood at the cupboard mirror: "Good morning. Did you know turtles lived with the dinosaurs?" Five times, each louder.
The first point went fine. At "how they lay eggs" she stopped. Blank. Again. Blank.
So she wrote "EGGS ON THE BEACH" on a small card and practised until she didn't need to look.
On Monday she came home and said, "I only looked at the card once."

qa.q: What did Deepika write on the small card?
What might Deepika's going blank twice at the same point suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: She was probably nervous and frustrated, but it showed her exactly where she needed help.

qa.q: What else could Deepika try when rehearsing her next talk?
qa.a: She could practise in front of a family member, so it feels more like speaking to a real audience.

qa.q: How might Jeevan see his sister's practice?
qa.a: Jeevan seems curious and a bit impressed, watching her imagine the class and fix the spot where she kept forgetting.

grounding: It shows a girl imagining the classroom, practising her opening line in front of the mirror, and noticing where she forgets the second point.

subtype: Approach: rehearses a speech in the mind and in front of a mirror [Action]
passage:
Thursday. Aditi's class talk on the water cycle was on Monday. In bed, she pictured it: walking to the front, thirty faces looking up. Her stomach flipped.
Friday. At the bathroom mirror she practised her first line. "Every raindrop you've seen was once part of the sea." Slow, fast, smiling. Her brother Madhav banged on the door. "Are you talking to yourself?"
"Practising!"
Saturday. She did the whole talk into the mirror. After "evaporation," her mind went blank. Again. Blank at the same place.
She drew a tiny cloud on the back of her hand. Cloud meant condensation. She practised three more times, glancing at it.
Monday. In front of the class, she looked at her hand once, and kept going.

qa.q: What did Aditi draw on the back of her hand?
qa.a: She drew a tiny cloud on the back of her hand.

qa.q: How did Aditi feel when she first pictured giving the talk?
qa.a: She felt nervous, with her stomach flipping as she imagined thirty faces looking up.

qa.q: What else could Aditi add to her practice, and why?
qa.a: She could practise once in front of Madhav, so she gets used to a real listener before Monday.

qa.q: How might Madhav see Aditi's practising?
qa.a: Madhav finds it funny at first, asking if she's talking to herself, without knowing it is helping her prepare.

grounding: It shows a girl imagining the classroom, practising her opening in the mirror, and spotting where she forgets the second point.
